title: Lord, Grant That We E’er Pure Retain
description: Lord, Grant That We E’er Pure Retain in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Ludwig Helmbold wrote these words in German. Matthias Loy's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 390.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, grant that we e’er pure re-tain The cat-e-chis-mal doc-trine plain As Lu-ther taught the heav-enly truth In sim-ple words to ten-der youth.

lines: Lord, grant that we e’er pure retain
As Luther taught the heavenly truth
In simple words to tender youth.
That we Thy holy Law may know
And mourn our sin and all its woe
And yet believe in Father, Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One.
That we on Thee, our Father, call,
Who canst and wilt give help to all;
That as Thy children we may live,
Whom Thou in Baptism didst receive.
That, if we fall, we rise again,
And take the Sacrament in faith.—
Amen. God grant a happy death!

licence: Public domain: Ludwig Helmbold died in 1598; Matthias Loy died in 1915.
credits: Words by Ludwig Helmbold (1532–1598), translated by Matthias Loy (1828–1915), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
